title: inspectMetadata
body:
## inspectMetadata

Read the camera-recorded metadata a set of photographs and XMP sidecars declares about itself into typed records: capture times and offsets, camera and lens identity, exposure, description, rights, GPS location and orientation. Each requested profile becomes a typed CSV that Calc can open as an editable workbook, and metadata.json keeps every source value, state and reconciliation for review. Independent host readers decode EXIF, GPS, IPTC and XMP from the captured bytes and are anchored against a fixed ExifTool listing; optionally the full native listing is published as native-observed evidence. It does not write, strip or decode images and certifies neither when, where nor by whom a photo was taken.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- A camera or editor can record a wrong clock, zone, place or owner; agreement between readers proves what the file says, not what happened.
- absent, unreadable, unsupported and ambiguous are different states; a null in the CSV has its reason in the State column.
- Sources that disagree are reported, not resolved: no source is preferred and no Metadata Working Group precedence is applied.
- GPS values are reported with the recorded datum text and no conversion; location, device identity and creator fields can identify people.
- A native listing is verified only when a trusted ExifTool is configured to replay it.

Native binding: `perl exiftool -config "" -json -a -G0:1:4 -n -e -u -q --System:all captured/ID.EXT... (fixed; every authored value is a catalogue ID, never a tag name or option)`. Output kind: `["text","table"]`.

Inputs: none.

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `media` | The set of photographs and XMP sidecar files to read: either an explicit list of items or one folder. Every item is captured into the run before any native process starts, and every scanned folder entry is listed in manifest.json as included or excluded with a reason, so you can see exactly which files were and were not examined. | `{"type":"union","options":[{"type":"object","properties":{"items":{"type":"array","required":true,"minItems":1,"maxItems":512,"items":{"type":"object","properties":{"id":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":32,"required":true},"path":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":4096,"required":true},"sha256":{"type":"string","minLength":64,"maxLength":64},"sidecar":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":4096}}}}}},{"type":"object","properties":{"folder":{"type":"object","required":true,"properties":{"path":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":4096,"required":true},"extensions":{"type":"array","minItems":1,"maxItems":11,"uniqueItems":true,"items":{"type":"enum","values":[".jpg",".jpeg",".xmp",".tif",".tiff",".dng",".png",".webp",".heic",".heif",".avif"]}},"depth":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":2},"maxItems":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":512},"sidecars":{"type":"enum","values":["none","adjacent"]}}}}}]}` | **required** |
| `profiles` | Which groups of catalogued fields to assess: capture, device, exposure, description, rights, location and rendering. Fields outside the selected profiles are unassessed, neither read nor claimed absent. inspectMetadata writes one typed CSV per profile. | `{"type":"array","minItems":1,"maxItems":7,"uniqueItems":true,"items":{"type":"enum","values":["capture","device","exposure","description","rights","location","rendering"]}}` | **required** |
| `nativeListing` | When true, also publish ExifTool's complete fixed listing of every captured file as native-observations.json (native-observed proof level). Verifying such a run needs a configured trusted ExifTool to replay it, otherwise verification reports NATIVE_REPLAY_UNAVAILABLE. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | omitted |
| `creatorInterpretation` | How the EXIF Artist string is read into the creator list on the read operations: literal (default, the original behaviour: one string) or mwg (split on "; " outside quotes, the Metadata Working Group creator list, with an Artist that does not re-join exactly reported as unreadable). Omitting it or choosing literal keeps every existing plan and result unchanged; mwg is what editMetadata always uses to read back creators. | `{"type":"enum","values":["literal","mwg"]}` | omitted |
